message.content:
In this repository, search for where the server sends outbound HTTP webhook/notification requests to external systems when content changes (e.g. a webhook dispatcher/sender function that does an HTTP POST to a user-configured URL). 

I need:
1. The exact function name and file path that performs the actual outbound HTTP request (the "delivery" function - e.g. something like sendWebhook, deliverWebhook, fireWebhook, notify, dispatch, etc.)
2. Any mechanism that validates/protects the target URL against pointing to internal/private network addresses (SSRF protection) - e.g. checks against private IP ranges (10.x, 192.168.x, 127.x, 169.254.x, link-local, etc.), DNS rebinding protection, or an allowlist. Give the exact file path and function/class name.

Search terms to try: "webhook", "SSRF", "private", "isPrivateIP", "internal", "loopback", "169.254", "127.0.0.1", "dns rebind", "fetch(", "axios.post", "http.request", "notification", "dispatch".

Report back file paths with line numbers and relevant code snippets (short, just the key lines) for both the delivery function and the protection mechanism.

- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review

    27		timeout = 30 * time.Second
    28	
    29		// safeClient is the shared HTTP client used for all webhook dispatches.
    30		// Its Transport guards against SSRF by blocking connections to reserved/private
    31		// IP addresses at dial time, which also defeats DNS rebinding attacks.
    32		safeClient = &http.Client{
    33			Timeout: timeout,
    34			Transport: &http.Transport{
    35				DialContext: safeDialContext,
    36			},
    37		}

    45				for payload := range asyncPostQueue {

    57	// safeDialContext is a net.Dialer.DialContext replacement that resolves the target
    58	// hostname and rejects any address that falls within a reserved/private IP range.
    59	func safeDialContext(ctx context.Context, network, addr string) (net.Conn, error) {
    60		host, port, err := net.SplitHostPort(addr)
    61		if err != nil {
    62			return nil, errors.Errorf("webhook: invalid address %q", addr)
    63		}
    64	
    65		ips, err := net.DefaultResolver.LookupHost(ctx, host)
    66		if err != nil {
    67			return nil, errors.Wrapf(err, "webhook: failed to resolve host %q", host)
    68		}
    69	
    70		for _, ipStr := range ips {
    71			if ip := net.ParseIP(ipStr); ip != nil && isReservedIP(ip) {
    72				return nil, errors.Errorf("webhook: connection to reserved/private IP address is not allowed")
    73			}
    74		}
    75	
    76		return (&net.Dialer{}).DialContext(ctx, network, net.JoinHostPort(host, port))
    77	}

    79	type WebhookRequestPayload struct {
    80		// The target URL for the webhook request.
    81		URL string `json:"url"`
    82		// The type of activity that triggered this webhook.
    83		ActivityType string `json:"activityType"`
    84		// The resource name of the creator. Format: users/{user}
    85		Creator string `json:"creator"`
    86		// The memo that triggered this webhook (if applicable).
    87		Memo *v1pb.Memo `json:"memo"`
    88		// Optional signing secret for HMAC-SHA256 signature. Not serialized to JSON.
    89		SigningSecret string `json:"-"`
    90	}
    91	
    92	// resolveSigningKey returns the raw HMAC key for a signing secret. Secrets using
    93	// the Standard Webhooks "whsec_<base64>" serialization are base64-decoded to their
    94	// raw bytes; any other secret is used as-is. It returns an error when a whsec_-prefixed
    95	// secret is not valid base64, so callers fail loudly instead of silently signing with
    96	// the wrong key (which would make every signature unverifiable by the receiver).
    97	func resolveSigningKey(secret string) ([]byte, error) {
    98		if rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(secret, "whsec_"); ok {
    99			decoded, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(rest)
   100			if err != nil {
   101				return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "signing secret has whsec_ prefix but is not valid base64")
   102			}
   103			return decoded, nil
   104		}
   105		return []byte(secret), nil
   106	}
   107	
   108	// GenerateSigningSecret returns a new Standard Webhooks signing secret in the
   109	// "whsec_<base64>" form, backed by 32 cryptographically-random bytes — comfortably
   110	// within the spec's 24–64 byte range.
   111	func GenerateSigningSecret() (string, error) {
   112		buf := make([]byte, 32)
   113		if _, err := rand.Read(buf); err != nil {
   114			return "", errors.Wrap(err, "failed to read random bytes for signing secret")
   115		}
   116		return "whsec_" + base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(buf), nil
   117	}
   118	
   119	// Post posts the message to webhook endpoint.
   120	func Post(requestPayload *WebhookRequestPayload) error {
   121		body, err := json.Marshal(requestPayload)
   122		if err != nil {
   123			return errors.Wrapf(err, "failed to marshal webhook request to %s", requestPayload.URL)
   124		}
   125	
   126		req, err := http.NewRequest("POST", requestPayload.URL, bytes.NewBuffer(body))
   127		if err != nil {
   128			return errors.Wrapf(err, "failed to construct webhook request to %s", requestPayload.URL)
   129		}
   130	
   131		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
   132	
   133		if requestPayload.SigningSecret != "" {
   134			key, err := resolveSigningKey(requestPayload.SigningSecret)
   135			if err != nil {
   136				return errors.Wrapf(err, "failed to derive signing key for webhook to %s", requestPayload.URL)
   137			}
   138	
   139			msgID := "msg_" + uuid.New().String()
   140			timestamp := strconv.FormatInt(time.Now().Unix(), 10)
   141	
   142			mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, key)
   143			mac.Write([]byte(msgID + "." + timestamp + "."))
   144			mac.Write(body)
   145			signature := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil))
   146	
   147			req.Header.Set("webhook-id", msgID)
   148			req.Header.Set("webhook-timestamp", timestamp)
   149			req.Header.Set("webhook-signature", "v1,"+signature)
   150		}
   151	
   152		resp, err := safeClient.Do(req)
   153		if err != nil {
   154			return errors.Wrapf(err, "failed to post webhook to %s", requestPayload.URL)
   155		}
   156		defer resp.Body.Close()
   157	
   158		b, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 1<<20))
   159		if err != nil {
   160			return errors.Wrapf(err, "failed to read webhook response from %s", requestPayload.URL)
   161		}
   162	
   163		if resp.StatusCode < 200 || resp.StatusCode > 299 {
   164			return errors.Errorf("failed to post webhook %s, status code: %d", requestPayload.URL, resp.StatusCode)
   165		}
   166	
   167		response := &struct {
   168			Code    int    `json:"code"`
   169			Message string `json:"message"`
   170		}{}
   171		if err := json.Unmarshal(b, response); err != nil {
   172			return errors.Wrapf(err, "failed to unmarshal webhook response from %s", requestPayload.URL)
   173		}
   174	
   175		if response.Code != 0 {
   176			return errors.Errorf("receive error code sent by webhook server, code %d, msg: %s", response.Code, response.Message)
   177		}
   178	
   179		return nil
   180	}
   181	
   182	// PostAsync posts the message to webhook endpoint asynchronously.
   183	// It enqueues the request for bounded asynchronous dispatch and does not wait for the response.
   184	func PostAsync(requestPayload *WebhookRequestPayload) {
   185		if requestPayload == nil {
   186			slog.Warn("Dropped webhook dispatch because payload is nil")
   187			return
   188		}
   189		select {
   190		case asyncPostQueue <- requestPayload:
   191		default:
   192			slog.Warn("Dropped webhook dispatch because the async queue is full",
   193				slog.String("url", requestPayload.URL),
   194				slog.String("activityType", requestPayload.ActivityType))
   195		}
   196	}

    11	// reservedCIDRs lists IP ranges that must never be targeted by outbound webhook requests.
    12	// Covers loopback, RFC-1918 private, link-local (including cloud IMDS at 169.254.169.254),
    13	// and their IPv6 equivalents.
    14	var reservedCIDRs = []string{
    15		"127.0.0.0/8",    // IPv4 loopback
    16		"10.0.0.0/8",     // RFC-1918 class A
    17		"172.16.0.0/12",  // RFC-1918 class B
    18		"192.168.0.0/16", // RFC-1918 class C
    19		"169.254.0.0/16", // Link-local / cloud IMDS
    20		"::1/128",        // IPv6 loopback
    21		"fc00::/7",       // IPv6 unique local
    22		"fe80::/10",      // IPv6 link-local
    23	}
    24	
    25	// reservedNetworks is the parsed form of reservedCIDRs, built once at startup.
    26	var reservedNetworks []*net.IPNet
    27	
    28	func init() {
    29		for _, cidr := range reservedCIDRs {
    30			_, network, err := net.ParseCIDR(cidr)
    31			if err != nil {
    32				panic("webhook: invalid reserved CIDR " + cidr + ": " + err.Error())
    33			}
    34			reservedNetworks = append(reservedNetworks, network)
    35		}
    36	}
    37	
    38	// AllowPrivateIPs controls whether webhook URLs may resolve to reserved/private
    39	// IP addresses. When true, the SSRF protection is disabled. This is useful for
    40	// self-hosted deployments where webhooks target services on the local network.
    41	var AllowPrivateIPs bool
    42	
    43	// isReservedIP reports whether ip falls within any reserved/private range.
    44	func isReservedIP(ip net.IP) bool {
    45		if AllowPrivateIPs {
    46			return false
    47		}
    48		for _, network := range reservedNetworks {
    49			if network.Contains(ip) {
    50				return true
    51			}
    52		}
    53		return false
    54	}
